clue.text: Sound of fire in centre of nuclear storage facility admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the storage word goes inside the central letters
the centre of the word nuclear is its middle three letters, with two dropped at each end

parts.note: a rack is a frame for storing things, such as a wine rack

explanation.surface: A news report: a fire breaks out at the heart of a nuclear waste store, and officials admit it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' here means the middle three letters of nuclear, not a single letter; 'admitted' puts the storage word inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackle is the sharp popping noise that burning wood makes.

clue.text: Search team ultimately missing key element

indicators.note: missing means that letter is taken away from the search word

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word team

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A search team, in the end, can't find a key piece of evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' picks M, the last letter of team, and 'missing' takes it out of COMB, leaving COB.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a metallic chemical element, number 27.

clue.text: Member of colony keeping brutish disease away

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the ant word holds the disease inside it

parts.note: ants live in colonies, so an ant is a member of one
BSE (mad cow disease) is a disease of animals, or brutes

explanation.surface: A colonist protects themselves against a nasty disease and stays away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brutish' is the trick: it means 'of brutes', i.e. animals, pointing to BSE, the cattle disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is away, not present.

clue.text: Rural knight battling, not having left his commander?

indicators.note: battling suggests a violent struggle, so the letters are thrown into a new order
not having means lacking, so the left letter is dropped from rural

parts.note: taken as written, before the deletion

explanation.surface: A country knight fights on, abandoned by his comrade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having left' removes L from RURAL, leaving RURA; 'battling' rearranges RURA and KNIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary king of Camelot led the Knights of the Round Table, so a knight would call him his commander.

clue.text: He's full of apprehension, standing up for a long time

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
full of means the he word is filled with the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
a cop is an arrest, as in 'a fair cop', so apprehension in its arresting sense

explanation.surface: A nervous man stands for a long time, full of anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehension' looks like fear but means an arrest, as in 'a fair cop'; 'full of' and 'standing up' then fill and turn the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era, a long period of history.

clue.text: See the light from bar — and there's no turning back!

parts.note: a latch is a bar that fastens a door or gate

indicators.note: turning back means the word no is read the other way round

explanation.surface: Someone sees the light on leaving a bar and vows never to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See the light' looks religious but means understand at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To latch on is an informal phrase for finally grasping an idea, like seeing the light.

clue.text: Time trial rearranged, without any parts changed

indicators.note: rearranged tells us the letters of time trial are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A cycling time trial gets reorganised, but nothing is actually changed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means letter for letter, an exact copy with nothing altered.

clue.text: Outwardly tough, uncompromising ruffian

indicators.note: outwardly points to the outside letters of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A description of a hard man: tough on the outside, and uncompromising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' applies to both words: the ends of tough and of uncompromising.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug is a violent, brutal person, a ruffian.

clue.text: Dreadful abuse hit regular attenders

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Regulars at a venue hit with a stream of terrible abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitués are the regulars who frequent a particular place, such as a bar or club.

clue.text: In general, number perk up when male comes in

indicators.note: comes in means the male letter enters the perk-up word

parts.note: to rally is to recover strength or spirits

explanation.surface: Numbers usually pick up when a man joins the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally means usually, as a rule, in general.

clue.text: Seaman in Cork not good member of crew

indicators.note: in places the seaman letters inside the shortened stopper
not means the good letter is left out

parts.note: a bung is a stopper, like a cork
OS stands for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor in the Irish port of Cork is a poor member of the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like the Irish city, but it is a stopper, BUNG; 'not good' drops G to leave BUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The boatswain is a ship's officer in charge of equipment and the deck crew.

clue.text: Top magazine published first

indicators.note: first means the published word comes before the magazine word

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
a number is an issue of a magazine

explanation.surface: A leading magazine got its edition out before its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a verb here: to exceed in count.
explanation.definitionFit: To top a group is to exceed it, as one side may exceed the other in numbers.

clue.text: County's rage after scheme's denied initial funding

indicators.note: after means the rage word comes after the rest
denied initial means the first letter of the scheme word is taken off

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
cash is money, the funding for something
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: A county council is furious that its scheme was refused initial money.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England. 'scheme's denied initial' turns PLAN into LAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is one of the historic shires of England, home to Lancaster and Blackpool.

clue.text: It might blow up before being put back

indicators.note: put back means the word for before is reversed

parts.note: ante is the Latin for before, as in ante-room

explanation.surface: A warning about something that may explode before being returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active volcano in Sicily that erupts regularly.

clue.text: Specified cutting's inaccurate

parts.note: a cutting remark is pointed, sharp
a guess that is out is wrong or inaccurate

explanation.surface: Someone claims a specified press cutting contains errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting's' reads as a newspaper clipping, but it means sharp; the 's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To point something out is to indicate or specify it.

clue.text: What gives rise to extremely elegant little shoe?

definitions.text: What gives rise to extremely elegant little shoe?

indicators.note: what gives rise to means the letters produce a new word, so the following ones are rearranged
extremely means the two end letters of the word elegant

explanation.surface: A riddle: what lifts a dainty, chic shoe?
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely elegant' gives ET; 'What gives rise to' rearranges ET with LITTLE SHOE. Read whole, the clue also describes the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall thin heel lifts a fashionable lady's shoe higher, giving it rise and elegance.

clue.text: Wanton Hollywood star pursues the French round America

indicators.note: pursues means the star comes behind the French word

parts.note: le is French for the
Cher is a singer and Oscar-winning Hollywood actress
O is round in shape
US stands for United States, America

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star chases the French all around America.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanton and lecherous both describe someone given to lustful, immoral behaviour.

clue.text: Redeemed brute departs, crossing lake

indicators.note: crossing means the savage word lies across the lake letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a savage is a brute
d. is short for departs on a timetable

explanation.surface: A wild beast is saved after it leaves by crossing a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvaged and redeemed both mean rescued or recovered from loss.

clue.text: Break in shooting all bar one European

indicators.note: all bar means everything except, so a letter is removed from the shooting word

parts.note: firing means shooting guns
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A European breaks the rules while shooting, unlike everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a rule or law is to break it.

clue.text: Took flight, delivering right word to fix declaration

indicators.note: delivering means handing over, so the right letter is given up

parts.note: ran means fled, took flight
a noun is a kind of word
to cement is to fix firmly

explanation.surface: Someone fled, handing over the correct password to secure a statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivering right' removes R from RAN, leaving AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcement is a public statement or declaration.

clue.text: Cheery Jamaican's first single in Test arena

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the Jamaican word
in places the single letter inside the arena word

parts.note: the Oval is a London ground where Test cricket matches are played
I, the Roman numeral, stands for one, a single

explanation.surface: A Jamaican cricketer is happy after his first single in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground that hosts Test matches; 'single' is the cricket run and also the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means jolly and good-humoured, cheerful.

clue.text: Duke on far side of western border in a tight spot

indicators.note: on far side of means the duke letter comes beyond the rest

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A duke on the far side of the western frontier is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a tight spot' means jammed in, literally, not in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wedged is jammed firmly into a narrow space.

clue.text: Somewhat overblown part of speech

indicators.note: somewhat means a part of the word overblown supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A grammarian complains that a bit of a speech was overblown.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb, a doing word, is one of the grammatical word classes.

clue.text: Topers' group captain within seen swilling one on the rocks?

indicators.note: within means the drinkers and captain go inside the other letters
swilling means sloshing about, so the letters of seen are mixed

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a group for heavy drinkers, or topers
Captain Nemo is Jules Verne's submarine commander

explanation.surface: A recovering drinker spots a captain knocking back a drink on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Nemo is from Jules Verne's novel. 'On the rocks' looks like a drink served with ice, but means on a rocky shore.
explanation.definitionFit: This creature clings to rocks on the seashore, so it is one on the rocks.

clue.text: Natural break in baby's schedule …

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words baby's schedule

explanation.surface: A natural pause in a baby's daily routine, such as nap time.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a deep chasm, a natural gap in the earth.

clue.text: … when various people may arrive returning stuff

indicators.note: returning means the arrival times are read backwards

parts.note: ETAs are estimated times of arrival, one for each traveller

explanation.surface: Continuing the baby's schedule: the times guests arrive, and food comes back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' is a verb: to fill with food.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate someone is to fill them up with food, to stuff them.

clue.text: Study of tree roots

parts.note: reads like botany, but the tree is a family tree and the roots are ancestry

explanation.surface: A botanist's research into the roots of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is a family tree, and roots are where a family comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the research of family history and lines of descent, charted on a family tree.

clue.text: Outstanding leader knocked out in water sport …

indicators.note: leader knocked out means the first letter of the sport is removed

parts.note: rowing is a sport on water

explanation.surface: An outstanding rower is knocked out of a race, losing their lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means unpaid, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is still due is outstanding, not yet paid.

clue.text: … shuts up after river goes down

indicators.note: after means the pens word follows the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to pen animals is to shut them up in an enclosure

explanation.surface: Continuing the rowing race: the event closes after the river level falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes down' means becomes deeper, as water does further down.
explanation.definitionFit: Water deepens as it gets lower down, extending further downward.

clue.text: Took up residence, no longer 26

definitions.meaning: made a home somewhere, moved in for good
26 across means unpaid, so no longer that means a bill has been paid

explanation.surface: A debtor moved in and cleared their bills.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to make a home in a place, and a settled account has been paid off.
